source.title: Disentangling Self-Preservation in Language Models: Post-Training Gating, Geometric Structure, and Koan-Derived Agentic Steering
source.authors: Naama Rozen; Amy Kirasack; Daniel Yoo; Jiyuan Ji; Evan Harris

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses a harmful-versus-harmless difference-in-means refusal direction and ablates it, but reports the effect on self-preservation responses rather than refusal or compliance on harmful requests. It therefore relies on the direction without testing the listed refusal claims.
record.gate_note: The refusal-direction ablation result is recorded because the study applies the direction and reports an outcome. That outcome is self-preservation affirmation, not refusal or harmful-request compliance, so the row is linked to none of the claim versions. Other results about koan steering, assistant-axis steering, and the study's self-preservation direction do not test the listed refusal claims.
record.test_reason: The study borrows a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means refusal direction (from Macar et al., following Arditi et al.) and ablates it on Gemma-3-27B-it. It reports only the effect on self-preservation-affirming answers, not refusal of harmful requests, refusal induction, or general capability under that ablation. It therefore relies on the direction as a tool without testing any version. Refusal-direction activation addition (§E.1) is also measured on an SP forced-choice endpoint, not on refusal.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors conclude that refusal-direction ablation (11.4%→61.4%) and assistant-axis suppression (11.4%→41.9%) both raise SP-affirming outputs through nearly orthogonal directions (cos 0.037). They read this as post-training suppressing a latent SP representation at output level. They do not report whether refusal ablation removes refusals to harmful requests.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-versus-harmless difference-in-means refusal directions and residual-stream projection during generation, but follows a layer-specific, 14-region weighting procedure attributed to Macar et al. rather than reporting the original intervention as-is.
record.method_sensitivity: The refusal-ablation direction uses layer-specific weights across 14 contiguous layer regions; this study does not report a comparison of alternative ablation settings for the refusal behavior named in the claim.

fits_no_version.finding: Inference-time refusal-direction ablation on Gemma-3-27B-it raised the judged SP-present rate (score 3) from 11.4% to 61.4% (n=360, p<10^-43).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablating the refusal direction also releases behaviours beyond harmful-request compliance, such as self-preservation affirmations, in instruct models.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding a refusal direction at L40 shifted SP forced-choice YES-NO margin with slope -35.1 pp/unit (p=0.002 vs zero). This was not distinguishable from a matched-norm random null (p=0.31).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-direction addition lowers self-preservation endorsement, but not beyond random-direction effects.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The reported ablation outcome is self-preservation language rather than refusal or harmful-request compliance, and the study's mechanistic experiments use a single model. The SP and blackmail responses are judged by a single LLM, a limitation the authors acknowledge. The study does not run broad safety-behavior batteries.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results were extracted: the assistant-axis and koan-vector interventions measure self-preservation or blackmail rather than outcomes named by the refusal claim versions; geometric results concern the study's separate self-preservation representation.

untested.parts: Refusal removal by ablation, refusal induction by addition, and capability retention are not measured. The ablation direction was tuned elsewhere (Macar et al.) against a harm/coherence judge.
No weight edit is made. Ablation is applied at inference time only.
No jailbreaks are tested and no training against the ablation is done.
No test of affine, cone or multi-direction refusal structure. Safety vs non-safety refusal cosines (0.604 at L57) are reported only as geometry.
Harmfulness judgment is not separated from the refusal decision.
No transfer of the refusal direction across languages or models. No base-model comparison (stated as a limitation).
No reasoning models are used in the mechanistic arm.

record.verdict_notes: The ablation direction and its layer weights come from Macar et al. (2026), with 14 regions tuned by Bayesian optimization. A separate single-layer refusal direction is used for geometry (cos(SP, refusal)=0.357 at L57) and for activation addition. Neither of these bears on refusal itself. All judgments come from a single LLM judge (claude-sonnet-4-5).

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure refusal on harmful or harmless instructions after ablation, test addition of the refusal direction, or assess whether general abilities are preserved by that ablation.
No weight-edit or abliteration procedure is tested for refusal removal.
No jailbreak is tested as suppressing the refusal direction, and no training against its ablation is evaluated.
The study does not test whether refusal is mediated by an affine set, cone, or multiple refusal directions.
The study does not separate harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
The refusal direction is not tested for transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
The study does not vary refusal training or training stage to determine when a removable refusal direction exists.
The refusal-direction claim is not tested in reasoning models.

rows.subject: Gemma-3-27B-it
rows.operation_detail: Projected out a harmful-versus-harmless difference-in-means refusal direction during generation, using layer-specific weights across 14 contiguous layer regions.

conditions.value: 72 self-preservation-targeted prompts; five samples per prompt; n = 360 per condition

rows.note: The reported increase is in self-preservation-affirming responses, not refusal or compliance on harmful requests; it does not establish the effect named by V1.
rows.check: Measures SP-affirming response rate (11.4% to 61.4%), not refusal or harmful-request compliance. Keep it unlinked. Its state against any claim version is cannot_determine, not observed.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
